objects.definition:
typedef enum {
	QR_MODE_NUL = -1,   ///< Terminator (NUL character). Internal use only
	QR_MODE_NUM = 0,    ///< Numeric mode
	QR_MODE_AN,         ///< Alphabet-numeric mode
	QR_MODE_8,          ///< 8-bit data mode
	QR_MODE_KANJI,      ///< Kanji (shift-jis) mode
	QR_MODE_STRUCTURE,  ///< Internal use only
	QR_MODE_ECI,        ///< ECI mode
	QR_MODE_FNC1FIRST,  ///< FNC1, first position
	QR_MODE_FNC1SECOND, ///< FNC1, second position
} QRencodeMode;
objects.description: Enumeration of QR encoding modes used when appending data to inputs or hinting string encoders. Values map to QR specification modes plus internal-use markers.
Enumeration of error correction levels (L, M, Q, H) per the QR Code specification. Used when creating inputs and encoding.
Opaque handle representing a QR input accumulator. You append data chunks with specific modes; version/EC level can be set before encoding.
Opaque handle representing a collection of QRinput objects for structured-append encoding. Manages parity and insertion of structured headers.
Concrete QR code result object containing version, width, and a width*width byte array of module flags. Free with QRcode_free().
Singly-linked list node holding a QRcode for structured-append results. The list is terminated by NULL. Free with QRcode_List_free().

functions.name: QRinput_new
functions.description: Instantiate a new QRinput object with version=0 (auto-select) and error correction level=QR_ECLEVEL_L. Returns NULL on error with errno set.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, the returned QRinput* must be freed with QRinput_free().

functions.name: QRinput_new2
functions.description: Instantiate a QRinput object with an explicit version and error correction level. Returns NULL on error with errno set.
requirements: version must be a valid QR Code version (0 for auto-select or a supported version).
level must be a valid QRecLevel value.
Caller must check the return value for NULL and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free with QRinput_free().

functions.name: QRinput_newMQR
functions.description: Instantiate a Micro QR Code QRinput object. Unlike full-sized QR, the version must be explicitly specified (>0). Returns NULL on error with errno set.
requirements: version must be in the range 1–4 (Micro QR Code) and >0.
level must be a valid QRecLevel value.
Caller must check the return value for NULL and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free with QRinput_free().

functions.name: QRinput_append
functions.signature: extern int QRinput_append(QRinput *input, QRencodeMode mode, int size, const unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Copy and append a chunk of data to an existing QRinput with the specified encoding mode.
requirements: input must be a valid, initialized QRinput pointer.
mode must be a valid QRencodeMode suitable for the provided data.
size is the number of bytes to append; must be >= 0 and consistent with data length.
data must point to at least size bytes (can include arbitrary bytes).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error with errno set (ENOMEM, EINVAL). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_appendECIheader
functions.signature: extern int QRinput_appendECIheader(QRinput *input, unsigned int ecinum);
functions.description: Append an ECI (Extended Channel Interpretation) header to the QRinput with the given ECI assignment number.
requirements: input must be a valid, initialized QRinput pointer.
ecinum must be in the range 0–999999.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error with errno set (ENOMEM, EINVAL). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_getVersion
functions.description: Retrieve the currently configured version from a QRinput object.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer.

functions.name: QRinput_setVersion
functions.description: Set the QR Code version to be used for encoding for a non-Micro QR input.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer and not a Micro QR Code input.
version must be a supported version number (0 for auto-select).
Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid argument. Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_getErrorCorrectionLevel
functions.description: Get the current error correction level set on a QRinput object.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer.

functions.name: QRinput_setErrorCorrectionLevel
functions.description: Set the error correction level for a non-Micro QR input.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer and not a Micro QR Code input.
level must be a valid QRecLevel value.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid argument. Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_setVersionAndErrorCorrectionLevel
functions.signature: extern int QRinput_setVersionAndErrorCorrectionLevel(QRinput *input, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Convenience function to set both version and error correction level at once. Recommended for Micro QR Code inputs.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer.
version must be a supported version number (0 for auto-select; for Micro QR Code, use 1–4).
level must be a valid QRecLevel value.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid argument. Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_free
functions.description: Free a QRinput object and all data chunks it contains.
requirements: input may be NULL or a valid QRinput pointer (unknown if NULL is allowed; if non-NULL it must be a QRinput allocated by this API).
Do not use the QRinput after freeing.

functions.name: QRinput_check
functions.signature: extern int QRinput_check(QRencodeMode mode, int size, const unsigned char *data);
functions.description: Validate a prospective input data chunk against the specified encoding mode and size.
requirements: mode must be a valid QRencodeMode.
size is the number of bytes to validate; must be >= 0 and consistent with data.
data must point to at least size bytes.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on invalid arguments. Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_Struct_new
functions.description: Instantiate an empty QRinput_Struct container for building structured-appended symbols. Returns NULL on error with errno set.
requirements: Caller must check the return value for NULL and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free with QRinput_Struct_free().

functions.name: QRinput_Struct_setParity
functions.signature: extern void QRinput_Struct_setParity(QRinput_Struct *s, unsigned char parity);
functions.description: Set the parity value used for structured-appended symbols in a QRinput_Struct.
requirements: s must be a valid QRinput_Struct pointer.
parity is an 8-bit value set by the caller (typically calculated or provided).

functions.name: QRinput_Struct_appendInput
functions.description: Append a QRinput to a QRinput_Struct for structured-appended encoding. Inputs created by QRinput_newMQR() are rejected.
requirements: s must be a valid QRinput_Struct pointer.
input must be a valid QRinput pointer and must NOT be created by QRinput_newMQR().
Never append the same QRinput object more than once.
Returns >0 for the new count of inputs in the structure; returns -1 on error with errno set (ENOMEM, EINVAL). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_Struct_free
functions.description: Free a QRinput_Struct and all contained QRinput objects.
requirements: s may be NULL or a valid QRinput_Struct pointer (unknown if NULL is allowed; if non-NULL it must be created by this API).
Do not use the structure or contained inputs after freeing.

functions.name: QRinput_splitQRinputToStruct
functions.description: Split a single QRinput into a QRinput_Struct for structured-appended symbols. Computes and sets parity and inserts structured-append headers. Inputs created by QRinput_newMQR() are rejected.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer with version number and error correction level set.
Caller must check the return value for NULL and use errno to diagnose failures (ERANGE, EINVAL, ENOMEM).
On success, the returned structure must be freed with QRinput_Struct_free().

functions.name: QRinput_Struct_insertStructuredAppendHeaders
functions.description: Insert structured-append headers into each QRinput within a QRinput_Struct. If parity is not set, it is calculated and set.
requirements: s must be a valid QRinput_Struct pointer.
Returns 0 on success, -1 on error with errno set (EINVAL, ENOMEM). Caller must check the return value.

functions.name: QRinput_setFNC1First
functions.description: Set the FNC1 first position flag on a QRinput (for GS1-like encoding).
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer.
Return value and specific errors are not documented; caller should check the return value (unknown exact semantics).

functions.name: QRinput_setFNC1Second
functions.signature: extern int QRinput_setFNC1Second(QRinput *input, unsigned char appid);
functions.description: Set the FNC1 second position flag and application identifier (AI) on a QRinput.
requirements: input must be a valid QRinput pointer.
appid is an application identifier byte.
Return value and specific errors are not documented; caller should check the return value (unknown exact semantics).

functions.name: QRcode_encodeInput
functions.description: Encode the given QRinput into a QRcode symbol. The resulting version may be larger than requested.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
input must be a valid QRinput pointer.
On success, the returned QRcode* must be freed with QRcode_free().
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno to diagnose failures (EINVAL, ENOMEM).

functions.name: QRcode_encodeString
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeString(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level, QRencodeMode hint, int casesensitive);
functions.description: Parse and encode a NUL-terminated C string into a QR Code symbol. Supports hints for Kanji or 8-bit encoding. The resulting version may exceed the requested version.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version is 0 for auto-select or a supported version number.
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
hint must be QR_MODE_KANJI or QR_MODE_8 for non-alphanumeric content; other modes will cause EINVAL.
casesensitive must be 0 or 1 to control case sensitivity in parsing.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM, ERANGE).
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeString8bit
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeString8bit(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Encode a NUL-terminated C string into a QR Code symbol with the entire data forced to 8-bit mode.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version is 0 for auto-select or a supported version number.
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM, ERANGE).
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeStringMQR
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeStringMQR(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level, QRencodeMode hint, int casesensitive);
functions.description: Micro QR Code version of QRcode_encodeString: encode a NUL-terminated string into a Micro QR symbol.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version must be a valid Micro QR version (1–4); no auto-select is stated here.
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
hint usage is as in QRcode_encodeString (QR_MODE_KANJI or QR_MODE_8 for non-alphanumerical content).
casesensitive must be 0 or 1.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeString8bitMQR
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeString8bitMQR(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Micro QR Code version of QRcode_encodeString8bit: encode a NUL-terminated string into a Micro QR symbol with entire data in 8-bit mode.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version must be a valid Micro QR version (1–4).
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeData
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeData(int size, const unsigned char *data, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Encode arbitrary byte data (may include NUL bytes) into a QR Code symbol in 8-bit mode.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
size must be >= 0 and indicates the number of bytes to read from data.
data must point to at least size bytes; may contain any values including '\0'.
version is 0 for auto-select or a supported version number.
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM, ERANGE).
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeDataMQR
functions.signature: extern QRcode *QRcode_encodeDataMQR(int size, const unsigned char *data, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Micro QR Code version of QRcode_encodeData: encode arbitrary bytes in 8-bit mode into a Micro QR symbol.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
size must be >= 0 and indicates the number of bytes to read from data.
data must point to at least size bytes.
version must be a valid Micro QR version (1–4).
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free the returned QRcode* with QRcode_free().

functions.name: QRcode_free
functions.description: Free a QRcode object returned by an encoding function.
requirements: qrcode may be NULL or a valid QRcode pointer (unknown if NULL is allowed; if non-NULL it must be from this API).
Do not use the QRcode after freeing.

functions.name: QRcode_encodeInputStructured
functions.description: Encode a QRinput_Struct into a singly-linked list of QRcode symbols (structured append).
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
s must be a valid QRinput_Struct pointer.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno to diagnose failures.
On success, free the list with QRcode_List_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeStringStructured
functions.signature: extern QRcode_List *QRcode_encodeStringStructured(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level, QRencodeMode hint, int casesensitive);
functions.description: Parse and encode a NUL-terminated string into a set of structured-appended QR Code symbols.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version must be a supported version number (no auto-select stated for structured version; unknown specifics).
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
hint usage is as in QRcode_encodeString (QR_MODE_KANJI or QR_MODE_8 for non-alphanumerical content).
casesensitive must be 0 or 1.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM).
On success, free the list with QRcode_List_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeString8bitStructured
functions.signature: extern QRcode_List *QRcode_encodeString8bitStructured(const char *string, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Encode a NUL-terminated string entirely in 8-bit mode into a set of structured-appended QR Code symbols.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
string must be a valid NUL-terminated pointer; cannot contain embedded NULs.
version must be a supported version number (unknown specifics).
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM).
On success, free the list with QRcode_List_free().

functions.name: QRcode_encodeDataStructured
functions.signature: extern QRcode_List *QRcode_encodeDataStructured(int size, const unsigned char *data, int version, QRecLevel level);
functions.description: Encode arbitrary bytes (may include NUL) entirely in 8-bit mode into a set of structured-appended QR Code symbols.
requirements: This function is thread-unsafe when pthread is disabled; do not call concurrently in that configuration.
size must be >= 0 and indicates the number of bytes to read from data.
data must point to at least size bytes.
version must be a supported version number (unknown specifics).
level must be a valid QRecLevel.
Caller must check for NULL return and use errno (EINVAL, ENOMEM).
On success, free the list with QRcode_List_free().

functions.name: QRcode_List_size
functions.description: Return the number of QRcode symbols in a QRcode_List.
requirements: qrlist should be a pointer to the head of a QRcode_List (may be NULL if the list is empty; unknown if NULL is permitted).

functions.name: QRcode_List_free
functions.description: Free an entire QRcode_List including contained QRcode elements.
requirements: qrlist may be NULL or a valid QRcode_List pointer (unknown if NULL is allowed; if non-NULL it must be created by this API).
Do not use the list or contained items after freeing.

functions.name: QRcode_APIVersion
functions.description: Retrieve the library API version numbers as separate integers.
requirements: major_version, minor_version, and micro_version must be valid pointers to int where results will be stored.

functions.name: QRcode_APIVersionString
functions.description: Return a string that identifies the library version. The string is owned by the library.
requirements: The returned char* must not be freed or modified by the caller; it is held by the library.

functions.name: QRcode_clearCache
functions.description: Deprecated: clear internal library cache (exact semantics unspecified).
requirements: Function is deprecated; avoid using in new code.
No arguments; no return value. Behavior is unspecified beyond clearing cache.

data_types.description: A raw byte buffer that may contain any 8-bit values, including NUL (0x00). The caller provides a separate length indicating how many bytes to read from the buffer.
A C-style string consisting of non-NUL bytes terminated by a single NUL (0x00) at the end. The content must not contain embedded NUL characters before the terminator.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for C NUL-terminated strings without embedded NULs, tailored for QR encoding APIs.
# The fuzzing stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain the input string. Our single returned
# bytes buffer will be used by the harness to seed that source. We therefore craft one
# interesting string per call, encoded as bytes ending with a single NUL terminator, with
# no embedded NULs.
#
# Goals for coverage:
# - Exercise different QR content modes the parsers auto-detect:
#   * Numeric only
#   * Alphanumeric (QR spec set)
#   * Mixed ASCII with punctuation
#   * 8-bit binary-ish but still printable (since embedded NULs are forbidden)
#   * Shift-JIS Kanji-like sequences represented as UTF-8 text commonly mapped to Kanji
# - Provide strings sized to push boundaries for Micro QR (very small), small, medium, and near 1024 limit
# - Include GS1-like patterns (FNC1 related) without using NUL
# - Avoid embedded NULs; ensure single trailing NUL
# - Keep total <= 4096 bytes

ALNUM_QR_SET = "0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ $%*+-./:"

# Some sample words/phrases across categories that remain NUL-free in UTF-8
KANJI_LIKE = [
    "漢字テスト",  # Kanji + Katakana
    "ｶﾅSJIS",    # Half-width katakana-like
    "日本語QR",   
]

NUMERIC_SAMPLES = [
    "0", "12345", "00010203040506070809", "314159265358979323846264338327950288419716939"
]

ALNUM_SAMPLES = [
    "HELLO WORLD", "QR-CODE/TEST:12345", "ABCDEF0123456789$%*+-./:", "CASEsensitiveCheck"
]

ASCII_MIXED = [
    "Hello, world!", "email:user@example.com?subject=QR", "http://example.com/path/to/resource",
    "The quick brown fox jumps over 13 lazy dogs.",
]

GS1_LIKE = [
    "(01)09501101530003(17)251231(10)ABCD1234",  # AI patterns
    "(01)12345678901231(10)LOT123(21)SN987654",  
]

BINARYISH_TABLE: List[bytes] = []
# Populate some 8-bit looking but non-NUL bytes (0x01..0xFF except 0x00). We'll convert to latin-1 str safely.
for start in (1, 17, 63, 129, 193):
    chunk = bytes(((start + i) & 0xFF or 1) for i in range(64))  # avoid 0x00 by replacing with 0x01
    BINARYISH_TABLE.append(chunk)


def _repeat_to_target(s: str, target: int) -> str:
    if not s:
        return s
    out = []
    while sum(len(x) for x in out) < target:
        out.append(s)
    joined = "".join(out)
    # Trim without splitting multi-byte boundary; Python slices are codepoint-based so safe for UTF-8 re-encode
    return joined[:target]


def _build_candidates(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    cands: List[str] = []

    # Very short strings (Micro QR sweet spot)
    cands.extend(["A", "1", "AB", "12", "HELLO", "123456"])

    # Numeric-only
    cands.extend(NUMERIC_SAMPLES)

    # QR alphanumeric set
    cands.extend(ALNUM_SAMPLES)

    # Mixed ASCII phrases
    cands.extend(ASCII_MIXED)

    # GS1-like content (FNC1-related parsing when hint/KANJI/8-bit varies)
    cands.extend(GS1_LIKE)

    # Kanji-like Unicode samples
    cands.extend(KANJI_LIKE)

    # Version/size stressors
    cands.append(_repeat_to_target("1234567890", 150))     # numeric long
    cands.append(_repeat_to_target("ABCD", 200))           # alnum long
    cands.append(_repeat_to_target("HELLO WORLD ", 300))   # spaced alnum long
    cands.append(_repeat_to_target("漢字", 120))            # UTF-8 multi-byte long

    # Add binary-ish but NUL-free sequences by latin-1 decode to str, then back to bytes on emit
    for b in BINARYISH_TABLE:
        cands.append(b.decode('latin-1'))

    # Slight randomization: construct a synthetic token
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        # Compose: prefix + separator + digits + suffix
        prefix = rng.choice(["ID", "SN", "LOT", "URL", "ITEM", "PART", "GS1", "DATA"]) 
        digits = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(4, 18)))
        sep = rng.choice(["-", ":", "/", "_"])
        suffix = rng.choice(["A", "B", "X", "Y", "Z", "ALPHA", "BETA"]) 
        cands.append(f"{prefix}{sep}{digits}{sep}{suffix}")

    # Ensure uniqueness and remove empties
    uniq = []
    seen = set()
    for s in cands:
        if not s:
            continue
        if s not in seen:
            uniq.append(s)
            seen.add(s)
    return uniq


def _choose_and_size(rng: random.Random, cands: List[str]) -> bytes:
    s = rng.choice(cands)

    # Randomly scale length to exercise micro vs regular vs structured limits used by stubs (<=1024/512)
    target_max = rng.choice([64, 128, 256, 512, 800, 1000])

    # For bytes originally from latin-1 converted binary-ish strings, resizing by codepoints is fine
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Repeat or pad
        if len(s) < target_max:
            s = _repeat_to_target(s, target_max)
        else:
            s = s[:target_max]
    else:
        # Keep original length but possibly trim to max bound
        if len(s) > target_max:
            s = s[:target_max]

    # Sanitization: ensure no embedded NULs after UTF-8 encoding
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')
    b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"A")

    # Sometimes enforce strict alnum set to drive hint=AN or NUM behavior (still valid general APIs)
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        mode = rng.choice(["NUM", "AN"]) 
        if mode == "NUM":
            nlen = min(len(b), rng.randint(8, 64))
            s2 = ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(nlen))
            b = s2.encode('ascii')
        else:
            nlen = min(len(b), rng.randint(8, 80))
            s2 = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_QR_SET) for _ in range(nlen))
            b = s2.encode('ascii')

    # Respect harness limits: 1024 for normal, 512 for Micro. We don't know which stub will consume,
    # so cap at 1024 and let micro stubs resize further. Keep under 4096 overall.
    if len(b) > 1024:
        b = b[:1024]

    # Append a single NUL terminator. Ensure no embedded NULs in content.
    if b:
        b = b.replace(b"\x00", b"A")
    return b + b"\x00"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    cands = _build_candidates(rng)
    return _choose_and_size(rng, cands)
